title: IG2 coding evaluation: specifications 0.3 and 0.4
subtitle:
Prospective comparison | November 7, 2026
Independent coding, source review, and reconciliation complete

blocks.text: Assessment

The prospective comparison is complete: three source cases, two frozen coding specifications, three independent coders per condition, masked proposition alignment, two independent source audits, and coordinator reconciliation. All eighteen coding outputs survived the usage interruption. The reviewers resumed their saved contexts; no coding or alignment run was repeated.

Version 0.4 did not demonstrate better overall independent repeatability or fewer source-supported evidence-basis errors in this sample. On the same 42 matched propositions, the three coders agreed on all six common fields in 24 cases under version 0.3 and 21 under version 0.4. Agreement improved modestly for deontic force, remained unchanged for grammar, and declined for institutional type, governance level, and the Boolean dispute flag.

Source reconciliation identifies five evidence-basis error groups: one under version 0.3 and four under version 0.4. It identifies no interpretation-changing error or material extraction/qualifier omission in either condition. Those are bounded review findings, not proof of error-free coding. The richer version 0.4 schema exposes more identity and support claims to inspection, so the counts do not establish that it has a higher underlying error rate.

I would retain version 0.4 as the working representation because its separate support dimensions make claims easier to inspect. I would retain independent overlap and source-based reconciliation as part of the analytical method. The paper can demonstrate an auditable, review-assisted institutional reconstruction; this test does not support a claim that version 0.4 independently classifies every field reliably or outperforms version 0.3.
Cases and bounded outcomes

blocks.text: Primary source-review findings

Both reviewers examined all 18 annotations, 587 retained units, 327 relations, and 83 source entries, including unanimous claims. Reviewer A submitted 50 bounded findings; reviewer B submitted 12. These totals include alternatives and convention questions, so they are not error counts. Reconciliation maps every finding into 59 distinct issue groups: five primary errors, nineteen convention deviations, ten criterion ambiguities, twenty-four defensible alternatives, and one unresolved referent.

blocks.note: Groups identify distinct proposition or relationship issues within a case. A shared issue can affect several runs; those incidences are not independent errors. No interpretation-changing or material coverage-loss group was confirmed.

blocks.text: The coordinator treats P03 and P04 as evidence-basis problems because their stored links overstate full-proposition correspondence or reverse a defined relationship. The reviewers differed on whether these effects were substantive evidence errors or convention issues. Treating both as convention-only would reduce the version 0.4 count from four to two; treating an additional under-labeled action basis as an evidence error would increase it to five. Neither sensitivity treatment shows fewer evidence-basis groups under version 0.4. These small descriptive counts still cannot rank population performance.

P05 requires care: a later PR updated_at value does not prove that a particular body sentence changed. The problem is the unsupported earlier/later wording assertion. The source supports neither certainty about its original wording date nor certainty that the reverse order occurred.
What should remain unresolved

The most consequential unresolved distinction concerns recognition. In F01, a participant quotes the proposed minimum of recent non-EOL releases and says, “I tend to agree.” The record supports tentative assent to that quoted floor. It does not uniquely determine whether the assent treats it as an institutional standard, nor whether it endorses every qualification of the original formulation. Both reviewers preserve ordinary-assent and local-expectation readings. No count of agreeing coders can establish a binding or generally adopted policy from that passage.

F02 illustrates a different boundary. The integrated artifact contains the requested plural identifier, but the packet does not locate the original typo and its correction operation. Observing a resulting state and observing a transformation are different claims. The guide permits an observed act or artifact, so the bounded alternatives do not justify retrospectively imposing a missing before/after-history requirement.

Other differences concern the analytical layer: a request to perform an operational action can also advance a proposal about a recurring testing arrangement; an articulated technical method can remain a strategy candidate or an engineering suggestion; a question about future scope can leave a historical work report uncontested. The ledger preserves these alternatives rather than manufacturing a uniquely correct label.

The one unresolved referent concerns what the bot would ignore after a reaction: the review, comment, or listing. The likely interpretation can remain explicit as an inference. The source does not establish actual bot execution. A narrower downstream statement can describe the announced conditional response without choosing its software implementation referent.
Corrections and conventions

Most convention deviations concern parse_mode: coders sometimes mark a parse pragmatic even though the selected action is explicit and only recommendation force is inferred. Other deviations concern replacement-word presentation, repeated-quotation speech acts, a preferred purpose/condition representation, and the scope of the uptake relation label. These issues matter for comparable representations, but they do not automatically change the institutional interpretation.

Reconciliation does not automatically accept a reviewer’s preferred form. For example, a consistently inferred avoid-rushing predicate can preserve the same meaning as the literal not-rush predicate. The ledger retains that alternative. Likewise, a repeated quotation’s label should not simply copy a potentially debatable original label; the source-based speech-act convention must govern both.

The complete ledger retains the original reviewer diagnosis, the coordinator’s grouping and rationale, affected annotation/run IDs, exact evidence, and the required downstream limitation. Original annotations, independent agreement, and tested criteria remain unchanged. The eight bounded case conclusions use these limitations; the archive does not claim to contain a negotiated consensus annotation.
Independent agreement

The eighteen runs contain 587 retained units, including 314 statement occurrences: 155 under version 0.3 and 159 under version 0.4. The masked alignment assigns every statement exactly once to 56 groups: 48 one-to-one, four split/combined, and four unmatched groups. It records no unresolved alignment group. These are correspondence judgments, not source-validity findings.

blocks.note: Within-version matches require one corresponding statement from each of that version’s three coders. The common subset requires one-to-one correspondence across all six runs. Counts describe retained records; source review determines material omissions and meaning preservation.

blocks.text: Within-version comparison includes 46 propositions under version 0.3 and 44 under version 0.4, covering 138 of 155 and 132 of 159 statement occurrences, respectively. The common all-six comparison contains 42 propositions: 27 from F01, four from F02, and eleven from F03. It therefore concentrates heavily on the procedure case. The table below compares the same propositions under both versions.

blocks.note: Independent final coding, before external reconciliation. Alpha is a supplementary descriptive statistic. The figures do not measure accuracy, population reliability, or negotiated consensus. Dispute is only a Boolean projection; its target and substantive scope require source review.

blocks.text: All three coders match on all six fields simultaneously in 24 of 42 common propositions under version 0.3 and 21 of 42 under version 0.4. This composite is more demanding than agreement on any individual field and should not be compared directly with a conventional alpha threshold. Grammar remains unchanged; deontic-force agreement improves modestly on the common subset, while institutional-type and level agreement decline. These results do not support an overall repeatability improvement for version 0.4.

Category imbalance matters. Each version assigns 124 of the 126 common-subset grammar judgments to regulative and only two to constitutive. Thus, 41 of 42 propositions have unanimous grammar labels while nominal alpha remains approximately 0.496. This sample supplies little evidence about discrimination between grammar categories. Target-level judgments likewise concentrate on operational activity; the coders place the few collective-choice labels on different propositions, producing slightly negative alpha. A high raw agreement percentage therefore cannot establish reliable identification of the less common category.

Screening agreement covers 48 of 49 focal entries under version 0.3 and 47 of 49 under version 0.4. Exact-span triple matches total 40 and 36, respectively. Semantic correspondence recovers additional matches without requiring identical text boundaries. These results remain distinct from the source review’s assessment of omitted actions, missing conditions, and unsupported institutional claims. The alpha implementation reproduces the published nominal example in Hayes and Krippendorff (2007), including missing judgments, to the reported four decimal places.
What the sample does not test

The 314 statement occurrences receive 297 operational and 17 collective-choice target assignments; none receives a constitutional or epistemic target assignment. Observed-action assignments are likewise confined to those first two levels. These are repeated coding occurrences, not independent events. The cases therefore provide no validation of discrimination at constitutional or epistemic levels, or of analysis of later value-driven forks. No such extension was added to this evaluation.
Mechanical checks and repair burden

First-complete outputs passed their assigned mechanical checks in six of nine version 0.3 runs and four of nine version 0.4 runs. After checker feedback and one source-based self-review, the original final checks passed nine of nine and six of nine, respectively. The evidence archive retains every first output, checker result, repair log, and final output. Record changes measure workflow activity, not error severity, and the unequal schemas create different opportunities for change.

All three remaining failures concern version 0.4 in F01: nine revision-identity failures in total. The packet supplies revision and git_blob_sha fields while the checker expects revision_id and blob_sha; one additional commit identity appears in the serialized source metadata. A post-freeze diagnostic adds aliases and exposes that existing identity in copies, without changing source text or coding judgments. All eighteen outputs pass that diagnostic. The original workflow still records fifteen passes. This is a packet/checker integration defect, not evidence of semantic correctness or an institutional interpretation error.
Readiness for the methodology working paper

The completed record supports a bounded methods demonstration with transparent source selection, independent coding, explicit uncertainty, and a documented review stage. It does not require a new human-coded reference set merely to make that claim. It also does not support claims of human-equivalent accuracy, cross-model replication, automated policy choice, or measured time and cost savings.

For downstream use, apply the five primary corrections or claim restrictions, preserve the unresolved recognition and application boundaries, and avoid presenting one reconciled label as if all coders originally selected it. The current frozen annotations remain research outputs with known defects; the corrected case conclusions and adjudication ledger identify what can be used without those overclaims.

The next release should repair the packet/checker metadata mismatch and clarify only distinctions needed for the intended conclusions: proposal identity versus discussion identity, partial response versus full-proposition restatement, resulting artifacts versus observed transformations, and the same-actor profile convention. If those revisions support a claim of improved independent performance, they need a new prospective test. This completed comparison should remain the record of what version 0.4 actually achieved.
Human coding standards and agent reconciliation

For a structured codebook analysis with three coders, nominal Krippendorff alpha is a suitable field-level measure, accompanied by raw agreement, category frequencies, and extraction coverage (Hayes and Krippendorff, 2007). Common conventions treat approximately 0.80 as dependable and 0.667–0.80 as supporting tentative use. These conventions depend on the inference and consequences of error; they are not universal publication gates (Krippendorff, 2016–2017). No such threshold was added to this study’s frozen primary criteria. Alpha of 0.80 is not the same as 80% raw agreement. For this structured codebook task, report a measure for each commensurable field rather than one pooled score across unlike judgments.

Independent reliability and negotiated agreement answer different questions. Campbell et al. (2013) illustrate the distinction with combined-code agreement of 54% before negotiation and 96% afterward. Their result supports a reconciliation procedure, not a general acceptance threshold. Qualitative teams can discuss disagreements, document their decisions, and retain unresolved alternatives; reliability alone does not establish validity (O’Connor and Joffe, 2020).

Agents can follow this approach. After independent outputs freeze, they can exchange the disputed coding, exact source passages, and reasons; each can retain or revise its interpretation. A final record should distinguish a source-supported correction, an agreed convention, and unresolved alternatives. The discussion should not require unanimity, and source checking should include initially unanimous claims. Any codebook revision learned during discussion requires a fresh test if the paper claims improved independent repeatability.

This run completed independent source review followed by coordinator reconciliation. It did not measure negotiated agreement among the original coders and did not compare AI with human performance. A future agent discussion can preserve initial outputs, record each evidence-based revision or retained disagreement, and report final negotiated decisions separately. Agreement after discussion cannot retroactively improve the independent reliability statistic.
Why a working paper remains defensible

A defensible baseline can show what the method extracts, where independently generated interpretations converge, which decisions require reconciliation, and how sources constrain the final claims. Perfect independent agreement is unnecessary. Low or ambiguous agreement on institutional type or governance level should limit claims about those fields, rather than disappear behind a final consensus. Human judgment still determines research priorities and value tradeoffs; the analytical coding and source checking can remain AI-assisted and inspectable.
Design and evidence

This prospective comparison applies the frozen project coding specifications 0.3 and 0.4 to identical source packets. Version 0.4 changes the project’s evidence and representation conventions; it does not change the official Institutional Grammar 2.0 framework. The comparison concerns complete coding workflows, including their schemas and checkers, rather than the isolated effect of codebook wording.

The canonical corpus contains 25,508 Bitcoin Core pull-request records. A conservative inventory excluded 226 previously exposed or referenced PRs found in the retained project material. Eligible records contained 1,000–12,000 Unicode characters across the complete body, comments, reviews, and inline comments, including bots and quotations. The title and serialized metadata did not contribute to this size criterion. A frozen SHA-256 ranking selected one record from each of three metadata strata: procedure-related title, remaining merged contribution, and remaining closed-unmerged contribution. The procedure stratum took precedence. These are sampling proxies, not substantive governance classifications.

The selected cases are fresh relative to the retained project exposure inventory. Unrecorded prior inspection and model training exposure cannot be excluded. The evidence package retains the selection rules, candidate ranks, exclusions, selected corpus lines, hashes, and a verification script. No candidate was selected for a favorable coding result.

The packets preserve all 49 original entries, including empty entries, and add 34 common contextual entries. Supplements contain recorded outcomes, relevant patches, directly referenced commits, a contribution guide pinned to a recorded revision, and separate metadata for the explicitly referenced successor PR. All six coders for a case received the same packet bytes. Missing edit histories, thread referents, image contents, and unprovided documents remain evidence limits.
Independent coding and review

Each version received three independent runs per case, for eighteen annotations. Every run used a fresh context without parent conversation, earlier annotations, or other coders’ output. Dispatch alternated the two conditions within cases and rotated their starting order. All runs used the inherited primary configuration without a model or reasoning override. The interface did not expose a provider snapshot, seed, sampling parameters, token count, or cost; those fields remain null. This is a same-configuration comparison, not cross-model validation.

Each coder preserved its first complete annotation, received mechanical checker feedback, conducted one source-based self-review, and froze its final annotation and change log. Mechanical checks assess schema consistency, source offsets, references, and specified safeguards. They cannot establish whether an institutional interpretation follows from the cited source.

A separate alignment context received source packets and shuffled annotation aliases with direct classification fields withheld. Two fresh source-review contexts received the full aliased records and their assigned coding guides, without aggregate agreement scores or the other reviewer’s findings. Structural differences can reveal the applicable conventions, so masking is partial. The coordinator reconciled the independent review findings against the source and retains unresolved judgments. This source-review process provides revisable analytical judgments, not a human reference dataset or an accuracy standard.

The primary assessment distinguishes interpretation-changing errors, evidence-basis errors, and material coverage or scope losses. Counts concern distinct proposition/error/case groups; the ledger separately identifies affected runs. A shared error can affect both conditions. Convention deviations, defensible alternatives, and unresolved diagnoses remain separate. Every source entry, retained unit, relation, and outcome or mechanism claim enters the review, including claims on which all coders agree.

Agreement measures use the frozen correspondence between focal propositions. They report screening, exact-span matches, one-to-one semantic matches, and field-level unanimity. Split, combined, unmatched, and unresolved records remain visible in the coverage results. The common all-six subset permits comparison on the same propositions. The former scalar standing label and the new documentary/recognition/application profile do not receive a numerical crosswalk. A Boolean dispute flag also cannot represent the full scope of a challenge.

During execution, the author asked how human intercoder reliability would be assessed. A dated supplementary declaration added nominal Krippendorff alpha and pairwise agreement for the common categorical fields, before alignment or comparison of coded labels. These are supplementary descriptive measures, not prespecified acceptance thresholds. The analysis reports category distributions and undefined coefficients where all labels occupy a single category. Three clustered episodes do not support population reliability estimates, confidence intervals, or an AI-versus-human performance claim.
Interruption and continuity

A weekly usage interruption stopped the source reviewers after coding and alignment had completed. A recovery check reverified every frozen run input and output and the alignment mapping. Both existing reviewer contexts resumed from their saved work under the same isolation restrictions. No aggregate agreement, mask key, or other reviewer’s findings entered either review context. The archive retains the interruption checkpoint, resumption log, first-complete reviews, correction histories, and final freezes. The interface did not expose credit accounting, so no itemized credit explanation or efficiency estimate is claimed.
Replication files

The accompanying evidence archive contains frozen source packets, selected canonical corpus lines, selection and exposure inventories, both specifications and checkers, all eighteen first/final annotations and repair records, alignment and review inputs/outputs, all derived metrics, the reconciliation ledger, bounded case conclusions, and verification scripts. PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json and tools/verify_package.py support byte-integrity checks. The full 25,508-record parent corpus is not duplicated; its SHA-256 identity and the full-selection verification result are retained.

The original preparation and assembly scripts retain their historical workspace assumptions. Do not rerun masking or input assembly over the completed review directories. Run reproduction commands in a copy, because metric and check scripts write their results. README.txt lists the portable commands and external-corpus requirement.
